item.title: Research with Reach: Translating Evidence into Action for People and Work
item.content:encoded:
Tara S. Behrend, Michigan State University

Michael T. Braun, DePaul University

Nick Turner, University of Calgary

Chia-Huei Wu, King's College London

This special issue seeks empirical research demonstrating how evidence from industrial-organizational psychology translates into actionable improvements for individuals, organizations, and society. Submissions must provide clear pathways showing how findings inform decisions, policies, or interventions that stakeholders can implement, rather than simply identifying important workplace phenomena.

The issue prioritizes use-inspired research emerging from organizational challenges or practitioner collaborations, employing rigorous methods and articulating tangible impacts. Manuscripts should be contextualized within specific occupations or sectors, include applied deliverables such as implementation frameworks, and demonstrate broader societal contributions such as improvements in wellbeing, equity, or workforce development.

Submissions must articulate the problem addressed, research-based solution, and observed outcomes from implementation. Conceptual papers, reviews, and meta-analyses are unsuitable. Well-executed field-based work that meets the translational aims is welcome.

Appel publié par Personnel Psychology. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Culture and Behavior Change
  • Employee Well-Being and Societal Outcomes
  • Resilience and Recovery at Work
  • Psychological Recovery and Sustainable Performance
  • Work and Non-Work Integration
  • Evaluation of Advanced Testing Technologies
  • Algorithmic Decision-Making in HR
  • Human-Automation Teaming
  • AI and Work
  • Economic and Employment Transitions
  • Sustainable Work and Environmental Psychology

Timeline

  • October 1, 2026: Submission window opens
  • October 31, 2026: Submission deadline (8:00 p.m. U.S. Eastern Time)

item.title: Turning Implications Into Evidence: Actionable Solutions to Real-World Problems of Practice and Policy Based on Prior Academy of Management Publications
item.content:encoded:
Julian Birkinshaw, Western University

Thomas P. Lyon, University of Michigan

Denise M. Rousseau, Carnegie Mellon University

Majken Schultz, Copenhagen Business School

Mo Wang, University of Florida

Amid rising concern about the relevance of their contents, many scholarly journals mandate inclusion of a managerial implications section. This section may be relegated to a few paragraphs at the end of an article and comprised of speculative statements loosely connected to the paper's empirical or theoretical content. And there these unvalidated implications tend to remain, largely unaddressed in future research studies and having little relevance to practice or policy.

This special issue calls for original research that develops actionable solutions from previously published managerial implications. By developing actionable insights from underdeveloped or dormant implications, this special issue furthers the core function of any science: the development of a corpus of valid and reliable knowledge. An applied science has the added demand that knowledge be usable outside of academia.

Appel publié par Academy of Management Perspectives. Lire l'appel complet sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Developing actionable solutions from previously published managerial implications
  • Novel empirical or conceptual analysis of practice and policy implications
  • Real-world problems of practice and policy overlooked in managerial implications sections
  • Robust analysis providing specific guidance for practitioners and policy makers
  • Building on theory developed in Academy of Management journals to enrich and reveal nuances of their usefulness

Timeline

  • January 1, 2026: Call for papers opens
  • January 31, 2027: Submission deadline at 23:59 ET

Associate editors
